## Anthropogenic stressors contribute to change
<hr>
<br/>
<div style="float: left; width: 43%;">

- **Historical build-up:**
    + hunting and megafaunal extinctions
    + agriculture and domestication
    + urbanization and population growth

<br/>

- **Current trends (today's topic)** 
    + land use change 
    + pollution 
    + globalization

<br/>

- **Equivalent to a natural stressor if an organism's response is similar or identical**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:160px; LEFT:490px; WIDTH:590px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/stress.png">

## Land-use change levels up 
<hr>

- **Before the Anthropocene, human induced land-use change was mostly regional**
    + hunting, agriculture and increased urbanization (e.g., appalachia)
    + thus, natural habitat modification is not new
    
<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:260px; LEFT:100px; WIDTH:900px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/landuse.png">

## How have humans modfied 75% of the land surface?
<hr>

<div style="float: left; width: 55%;">

- **Agricultural intensity must match demand**

<br/>

- **Freshwater is a limiting resource**
    + >40% dedicated to agriculture
    + deep water sources are needed
    + water needs to be diverted

<br/>

- **Minerals and metals are needed for everything**
    + recent coal production in the US is an exception
    
<br/>

- **Natural ecosystems provide raw materials**
    + and get it the way of urbanization
    + timber industry in Appalachia also an exception
    
</div>

## Pollution in Appalachia: Point vs. Diffuse Sources
<hr>

<div style="float: left; width: 53%;">

- **Point Sources:**
    + Coal mines = acid mine drainage
    + Waste water discharge from pulp/sewage/chemical plants
    + Industrial sites → heavy metals

<br/>

- **Diffuse (Non-Point) Sources:**
    + Agricultural runoff → nitrogen, phosphorus
    + Logging roads → sedimentation in streams
    + Urban storm water → oil, trash, nutrients

<br/>

- **Many headwaters streams, vital for biodiversity and clean water, are degraded**
    + mussels, brook trout, and salamanders are particularly affected.
    + Contaminants pose risks to rural drinking water

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:600px; WIDTH:450px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/pollute.png">

## Humans are now connected worldwide
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 60%;">

- **The impacts of *globalization* on natural systems is huge**

<br/>

- **Humans move species around - for better or worse**
    + necessary for food systems
    + unintentional as part of trade (invasive species)
    + intentional with unknown consequences
 
 <br/>
 
- **Infrastructure of globalization also disrupts natural systems**
    + roads fragment landscapes
    + transportation pollutes
    + politics of trade divides wealth

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:615px; WIDTH:550px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/shipping.jpg">

## Without globalization, what would we eat?
<hr>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:180px; LEFT:0px; WIDTH:1100px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/crops.jpg">

## Appalachian Mountains are threatened by invasive species
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 51%;">

- **Loss of Keystone Species: Eastern Hemlock is being devastated by the Hemlock Woolly Adelgid**

<br/>

- **Forest Composition Shifts: Emerald Ash Borer is killing ash trees across Appalachia**

<br/>

- **Aquatic Impacts: New Zealand mud snail compete with native macroinvertebrates**

<br/>

- **Kudzu grows up to 1 foot per day, covering and shading out native trees, shrubs, and understory plants**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:615px; WIDTH:500px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/hemlock.png">

## Globalization has societal consequences in Appalachia, too
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 60%;">

- **Global competition in coal and timber industries led to economic decline.**
    + single-resource economies (coal in WV, textiles in NC, etc.) suffered mass layoffs as industries moved overseas.
    + high unemployment, poverty, and population loss, especially among young people.

<br/>

- **Community Fragmentation: Outmigration of youth weakens social cohesion and drains local talent**
    + rise in addiction, mental health issues, and breakdowns in public services 
    
<br/>

- **Walmart-ization wiped out many local businesses and reduces local economic resilience**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:180px; LEFT:680px; WIDTH:375px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/timber.jpg">

## How do stressors interact?
<hr>

- **<span style="color:darkred">Synergy</span>: when the total effect is *more* than the sum of the individual effects**
    + loss of sea ice from warming exposes more dark surface which absorb even more heat
    + canopy gaps created by emerald ash borers killing ash trees allows invasion by Japanese stiltgrass, tree-of-heaven (which attract spotted lantern fly).


<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:290px; LEFT:0px; WIDTH:1100px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/stress3.png">

## We measure current change since Industrial age...
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:0px; WIDTH:600px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/model2.png">

<div style="float: right; width: 45%;">

- **Global mean surface temperature has risen 1.1 degree C since late 1800's**

<br/>

- **How much is left to come?**
    + depends on continued *forcings*
    + we can predict (based on trends)
    + always some uncertainty

</div>

## Future climate change IS inevitable
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:160px; LEFT:20px; WIDTH:500px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/model3.png">

<div style="float: right; width: 50%;">

- **Roughly 0.7–0.8 °C in the last ~50 years, meaning surface warming is accelerating**

<br/>

- **How much is left to come?**
    + depends on continued forcing
    + we can predict (based on trends)
    + always some uncertainty

<br/>

- **Reference: 5°C of “natural” warming that took earth from an Ice Age to our modern interglacial world took 1600 years**
    + Contemporary climate change could reach the same 5°C change >10x faster

</div>
